instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it in a rice cooker or a covered pot.
Drain the 2 blocks of tofu and cut each one crosswise into 4 slabs about 3/4 inch thick.

Lay the slabs on a double layer of paper towels in one layer and cover them with more paper towels. Set a baking sheet on top with a couple of cans on it. Leave them to drain for 15 to 20 minutes, and change the towels halfway if they're soaked.
Meanwhile, make the sauce. In a small bowl, stir together the 3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp mirin, 3 tbsp sake, 3 tbsp water and a pinch of sugar.
Grate or finely mince the 2 garlic cloves and add them to the sauce. Cut the 2 tbsp butter into small pieces and add it too. It doesn't need to melt.
Thinly slice 2 of the green onions.
Spread the 1/2 cup potato starch on a plate. Press each tofu slab into it on both sides and the edges, and shake off the extra. Coat them right before they go in the pan, or the starch turns sticky.

Heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium until it shimmers. Lay in half the slabs with room between them. Cook them without moving for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp.
Flip them and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's golden too. Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels.
Add the last 3 tbsp oil and cook the rest of the slabs the same way.
Pour off the oil left in the pan and turn the heat down to medium-low. Add the sauce and stir for about 30 seconds, until the butter melts.
Put all the tofu back in the pan. Turn the slabs in the sauce for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's thick and glossy and clings to them. There should be very little left in the pan.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash of soy sauce.
Put the tofu on plates, spoon any sauce left in the pan over the top and scatter the green onions on it. Serve with the rice.
method_notes: All three press firm tofu, dust it with starch or flour, fry it until golden and finish it with a soy sauce based sauce. Contemplating Sweets, the lead, mixes soy sauce, mirin, sake, water, a pinch of sugar, butter and garlic, and glazes the fried tofu in it on medium-low; Kokoro Cares fries the tofu in salted butter and stirs in mentsuyu, sweet sake and garlic off the heat, and Norecipes salts and weights its tofu for an hour and glazes it in a ketchup and soy sauce sauce with crisp garlic and mushrooms. No version of this dish had 20 or more ratings. RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for Japanese, has only a sesame crusted tofu steak with a teriyaki sauce and no butter, which is a different dish, so it was left out and the lead is the version closest to this dish. This one doubles the lead for 4, cuts each block into 4 thick slabs instead of 12 small pieces and fries them in two batches.
